- No outbound internet from the inference cluster; updates must be scheduled and delivered offline.
- Hardware: you mentioned NVIDIA GPUs (details below).

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the docs. A few answers below and some clarifying questions.

Hardware (planned):
- 8x nodes with NVIDIA A100 80GB (PCIe) today; evaluating adding 4x H100 80GB next procurement cycle (Q2 2027).
- Driver/OS: RHEL 8.6; drivers currently on 470.x, but we can standardize to a vendor‑approved baseline for deployment.

Maintenance windows / upgrade policy:
- Quarterly major upgrades; monthly critical patches.
- Air‑gap policy: no direct internet outbound from compute cluster. We use an approved transfer station for signed bundles (USB or internal transfer device) that is scanned by security.

KMS / HSM:
- We have an on‑prem Thales HSM for key storage. We prefer to keep keys on‑site; cloud KMS is not allowed for production inference keys.

Audit/logging requirements:
- Retain all inference audit logs (request metadata, model version, timestamps) for 7 years. Logs need to be exportable to our Splunk instance in the DMZ when connectivity is established.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Do you support offline upgrades delivered as signed bundles that our security team can scan and validate?
2) Does Redwood provide a hardened offline installer image (SHA256 signed) and guidance for air‑gapped installs?
3) What's your approach to driver/kernel upgrades needed for H100 (if we introduce H100s later)?

Happy to meet Wednesday 12/3 1–2pm ET (10–11am PT) for the deep‑dive.

—John

Thanks John — good details, and thanks Marissa for coordinating. Short answers and proposed plan from the SE side: 

Q1 — Offline upgrades as signed bundles:
- Yes. Redwood supports air‑gapped upgrades using signed, versioned bundles. We publish SHA256 hashes and PGP signatures for all release artifacts. For strictly offline environments we can provide an encrypted installer bundle on physical media that your security team can verify.

Q2 — Hardened offline installer image:
- We provide an installer image (bootable Linux appliance) with the Redwood runtime, model artifacts (if requested), and a signed upgrade manager. The image is validated via signature and hash before install. The runbook covers checksums and verification steps.

Q3 — Driver/kernel upgrades for H100:
- We recommend pinning to vendor‑validated driver versions. For H100 we support CUDA 12.x and the corresponding driver stack; we will work with your infra team to test upgrades in a staging cluster before production. Offline driver packages can be included in the signed bundle.

Additional notes:
- Minimum supported cluster for production latency SLOs: 4 nodes with A100 80GB (we see most customers start at 4–8 nodes). We'll produce a sizing worksheet tailored to your expected QPS.
- KMS/HSM: we support integration with on‑prem HSMs (PKCS#11) and can keep encryption keys on‑site; Redwood control plane components that require-key-management can be configured to use your HSM endpoint via our private connector.
- Logs: we can write audit logs locally to disk with configurable retention; when connectivity exists we push to your Splunk endpoint (we support batched, authenticated pushes to a DMZ collector).

Next steps (proposal):
1) Technical deep‑dive Wed 12/3 10–11am PT — we will present the offline install flow and sample signed bundle.
2) Post‑call — Redwood to produce a 2‑page Ops runbook (air‑gap install, upgrade, rollback) and a sizing worksheet by Fri 12/5.
3) Workshop — optional onsite or virtual 1‑day workshop to validate a dry‑run in staging.

Marcus — can you prepare a one‑page comparison of Dedicated vs Private (ops, costs, control) for John/Aisha to help with procurement conversations?

Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
